   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Bill Coats, STRATHCLYDE

Dear Brian/Ron/Chris,

Re Bill Clark's letter in Outlet
No. 80 about 'hidden messages'
in the +3 ROM, to arrive at
"Test Screen" you first hold
down the BREAK key then push the
'Reset' button. This is a screen
of different coloured numbers
against different coloured back-
grounds. If you now press keys
QAZPLM together you arrive at
the manufacturer's "RAM DATA
TEST" with the warning that your
discs can be corrupted from here
on.

When the +3 is switched on it is
in FORMAT LPRINT "E" mode.


Since Outlet No. 70 you have
been putting page numbers at the
foot of the letters pages, etc.,
[on TABLOID printout] and on my
set up (+3 and 120d+ printer)
the numbers need to be spread
out a bit to centre under their
particular pages. As I haven't
seen any correspondence about
this could it be a hiccup in my
computer or printer? Or is there
a poke(s) to rectify this?

All the best to "The Team".

                    Bill Coats

Brian Cavers to Bill Coats

Thanks Bill. I had long since
forgotten the "test screen" but
it now seems to ring a faint
bell.

The page number error is due to
my using condensed text mode
whereas TABLOID uses graphics
mode. I have rewritten the
routine using graphics mode
spacing so it should, in theory,
be the same proportionally on
everybody's printer. It is in
this issue for people to test.

                    Brian

From Dave Wood, CAMBRIDGE

Dear Ron & Brian,

Here are the +3 self-test rout-
ines...

Break + Reset. Tones & coloured
stripes. QAZ + PLM gives version
number. <E> takes you through
routines: RAM test, sound chip,
ULA test, keyboard, ULA sound
test, joystick test, cassette
output, screen switching,printer
test, disc drive test,tape test,
self-diagnosis.

BE VERY CAREFUL! After spin
speed test expects to FORMAT THE
DISC! Don't use a disc with data
on it!


From 128K BASIC: COPY RANDOMIZE
gives "Hello there - I'm a +3".
From timing screen AEU gives
tape test with animated blocks
of colour.VB goes back to BASIC.

Somewhere I've got some similar
data for the Spectrum 128 with
tape test but I can't find it at
the moment - probably someone
else is scribbling it down now!

Again, congratulations on the PC
OUTLET - it was worth waiting
for!
             Yours,

           Dave Wood

From John Chapman, NOTTINGHAM

Dear Brian

As you can see,I managed to get
Tasword 2 on +3 disk thanks to
you[OUTLETTERS 80]but the serial
8056 printer still will not
operate with it. When I go into
"Print text file" and just set
it to start on line 1 and print
to the end etc, all I get is the
message on the screen "press Q
to stop printing. The printer
stays quiet - not even a blip.
Maybe the +3 is sending the data
to the parallel - not the serial
port? When I press Q, nothing
happens - the program is locked
into the printing and I have to
reset the computer and reboot.


The link between Spectrum and
video or tv is via the RF (RF to
RF); this is why I can't get a
good and steady picture. The
connection from the RF on the
Spectrum to the video input on
the video doesn't work. The only
other conection is via the RGB
port but this is for a monitor
with composite sync so I haven't
tried this.

Looking through the list of back
issues (by the way, I haven't a
list from Outlet 72 to 77)I came
across SUOERPRINT in Outlet 64 -
an RS232 screen dump for 8056
printers. This might be what I'm
looking for (as well as for
Tasword Two) so I'm sending for
this issue.


Brian Cavers to John Chapman

Regarding the Tasword 2 printer
problem,first make sure you have
got FORMAT LPRINT "R" in line 15
as described in my reply in last
month's OUTLETTERs. Next, add a
"U" after the "R" so it reads:
FORMAT LPRINT "RU". I ommitted
this before although it should
not prevent printing and should
not be the cause of your problem
- it would simply prevent print
codes being sent.

Now include the following POKEs
in the same line as some +3's
have a bug...

POKE 23354,62 : POKE 23355,16 :
POKE 23399,20


Run and resave Tasword 2 again
using the menu option before you
try to print anything.

If it still locks up when trying
to print see if BREAK works and
let me know. Otherwise, reload
the program.Add the following to
the start of line 250...

LPRINT "testing 123";CHR$ 10;
CHR$ 13 : BEEP 1,1 :

There should be a couple of
RANDOMIZE USR commands following
on that line which does the Tas2
printing.

Run Tasword, enter a few xxx's
in the text file then try the
print.


You should get the "testing 123"
printed followed by the sound of
the BEEP (make sure your tv
sound is on) then followed by
the xxx's being printed.


Let me know exactly what results
you get.

To get video to video you need
to follow what I said before
about getting a cable. The RF
output should NOT be connected
to your video recorders VIDEO IN
socket.


Our back issues list is not up
to date but we hope to rectify
this as soon as possible.


Thanks very much for the music
which will appear in a future
OUTLET.

                    Brian

Donald Pemberton, CHESHIRE

Dear Ron and Brian,

I am stil running a Spectrum +3
and also a 48K+, both with Datel
+D drives. Each month I get your
OUTLET 3.5" disc version which
runs perfectly on both machines.
Prior to changing over to the
3.5" discs I used to get OUTLET
on 3" discs and took copies of
some items using the +D snapshot
button (key 4 - the 48K mode).
These run OK on the Spectrum +3
with the +D in 128K mode but not
on the 48K Spectrum + or the +3
in 48K mode.Do you know if there
is an answer to this problem? I
have no snapshot problems when
working from your 3.5" discs.


Thanks for all the work and the
long hours you spend in produc-
ing OUTLET.I look forward to its
arrival every month and now you
are producing a version for the
PC I shall look forward with
great interest to see the
result.I wish you every success.


        Yours sincerely,

       Donald Pemberton

Brian Cavers to Donald Pemberton

Thanks Donald.

When you load a file from the +3
disc then you must be in 128K
mode. If you then snapshot it to
the +D, even though you use key
4 to save a 48K snapshot, you're
actually saving a 48K image of
the machine in 128K mode as well
as the registers, flags, error
pointer etc for 128K.

The simplest way is to break in
and enter RUN 9982 which saves
to +D and uses far less space on
the disk. If when it reloads off
the +D it "hangs" or tries to
load from the +3 disc it may be
trying to load code, so...


Break in and note the line num-
of the break. LIST and examine
the line and note the filename
of the code. You need to copy
that too from the +3 disc to the
+D and then REMEMBER to alter
the syntax of that line to +D,
ie, LOAD d*;"name" CODE. To copy
the code you need...

10 CLEAR A-1
10 LOAD "NAME" CODE
20 SAVE d*"NAME" CODE A,L

You need to substitute the true
values for A, L and A-1. You may
find these in line 9984 in newer
issues but otherwise you need a
program like CATDB in Issue 76
or EXTENDACAT in 37.
                           Brian

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER



Dear Ron and Brian.

Your comment about the firm's
responsibility ending once they
have sent the goods with no
obligation to replace or refund
if they get lost, once again
raises an issue I have been
campaigning my MP and consumer
groups for some time to get laws
changed/introduced to give the
consumer (customer) far better
protection when dealing with
mail order firms. The following
is as it seems to me after some
years of delving into the
subject.


As OUTLET says, CHEZRON takes
responsibility for goods that
get lost or damaged; larger mail
order companies also in the main
do the same,the more responsible
companies large or small often
in the interests of customer
relations and to keep their good
name will also see the customer
right.

However, it seems there is not a
legal obligation do do so; it
depends on the firm's terms of
trading. "WHICH?", and two other
magazines, have in recent times
printed items that more or less
say if the customer does not
receive goods that have been
sent then tough luck! (put a bit
more politely but with same
message).

The following extract from the
OFFICE OF FAIR trading publi-
cation "GET SMART" on mail order
says it all.. "If goods get lost
after they have been sent to you
it is normally your loss
depending on on the carriers
terms but many firms will bear
the loss as a matter of good
will."

So once the firm hands goods to
the Post Office or any carrier,
their responsibility legally
ends (unless their terms of
trading says otherwise) it
seems. Note the above states
"carriers terms" so the only
course of action if the goods
get lost (or damaged) is to
claim from the carrier.


Again, this is a minefield as
such as the P.O. or Parcelforce
have different compensation
terms for different services and
if the sender did not use an in-
sured method of sending then no
compensation;also you need proof
of posting to make a claim. This
would have to be obtained from
the sender who probably did not
get one when posting.

Depending on the cost of goods,
one method would be to make the
sender prove they sent the goods
perhaps through the County Court
but with no guarantee of success
as if a person in Manchester
bought an item from a firm in
London then he would have to go
to London as CC hearings are
heard near the firm's address.

I have taken issue with the Post
Office and also brought the
matter to the attention of
consumer groups and my MP that
while it seems the law says it
is the customer's loss and
responsibility to make a claim,
the Post Office claims form asks
a lot of questions that the
customer cannot answer -only the
sender, ie, time and place of
posting,postage paid,how wrapped
weight, postal receipt and so
on.


To top it all the PO will only
pay compensation to the sender
unless the sender states in
writing otherwise.


I put it to Parcelforce that I
pay for goods plus the extra
compensation fee to send, the
goods get lost, the PO only pays
compensation to sender, sender
then refuses to replace goods or
refund so they have now been
paid twice for same goods and
the customer still has nothing.
"that's quite correct"say Parcel
Force, "that's our regulations".


I understand there is some EEC
proposal in the pipeline that
will make it law that a customer
does not have to pay for goods
until AFTER they have been
received - so no more having to
send money with the order.


This will go a long way to prot-
ect customers from lost/damaged
goods,firms that go bust or dis-
appear etc,but could cause prob-
lems to small firms who often
rely on taking in money before
sending goods to pay their way.
Plus it could cause problems if
people order goods then "avoid"
paying. I suspect pressure from
firms could well prevent this
from becoming law.The problem is
"good" firms could well suffer
due to the antics of "less good
firms". It would certainly stop
cases sometimes seen on TV and
in papers where it seems a"firm"
or individual sets up with the
sole intention of taking money
but not supplying goods and then
doing a runner.
.

You often see mentioned to only
deal with firms that belong to
one of the trading associations
or mail order protection schemes
but I find far too often the
magazine or firm selling what I
want - commonly in specialized
areas such as computers - do not
belong to any such schemes. Also
the schemes have so many "get
out" clauses you find your case
is not covered.


My MP says there is not a big
enough problem with mail order
firms to change law or introduce
better compensation schemes. (A
trading Standards Office said
they were not interested as I
did not pay them my Poll Tax!).


It is only the more spectacular
"complaints" that get publicity
in the press;only major or crim-
inal cases that reach the Office
of Fair Trading so,is the extent
of the problem really known? If
every time an unresolved problem
with a mail order firm cropped
up, ie, going bust,disappearing,
not sending goods, not replacing
lost/damaged goods etc resulted
in a complaint to an MP, the
scale of the problem could well
be put into better proportion. I
suspect many cases especially if
only few pounds are involved,end
in the customer suffering in
silence as it's not worth taking
legal action and no point at all
if a firm has gone bust.A letter
to an MP only costs a stamp.


The situation therefore seems
that if you send for goods by
post and actually receive them
then think yourself lucky and
give a big sigh of relief. If
you do not and the firm takes
the stand "not our problem" then
as said before, tough luck - it
seems it was your silly fault to
order by mail in the first
place. You're on your own unless
the firm actually committed a
criminal offence then TSO will
show some interest, If a civil
complaint - then little chance.
Even in one case where both the
TSO and Advertising Standards
both upheld a complaint re a
firm and reprimanded them,it did
nothing to help my problem or
get redress from the firm.


When I send an item by post or
any other method I ensure it is
covered by some form of insur-
ance relative to its value, ie
providing you obtain a "receipt
of posting",which is free at the
PO when you hand the item over,
it is covered up to about `22.
Higher cost needs special insur-
ance. It can often be better to
send by Parcelforce + insurance
even if small or light enough
for ordinary post.Obviously such
as OUTLET is impracticable to
hand over a hundred discs and
ask for a hundred receipts or
expect the PO to check a list of
100 addresses. It would also
probably cost more in time,
effort and extra postage to put
in a claim for a lost issue.


When buying anything and I do
not know if the sender provides
some form of protection or "good
will", I try and remember to ask
or insist it is covered by
insurance even though this may
put the cost up.


I have at times also insisted
the sender sends me the "proof
of posting" or insurance receipt
as proof they have sent it. This
has also proved beneficial in
the past as I have been able to
make the claim myself without
having to rely on sender.

P.W.JOHNSON, SADDLE HILL ROAD,
No. 1 R.D. DUNEDIN, NEW ZEALAND.

Greetings to all the team there
from NEW ZEALAND and congratul-
ations on the mighty effort you
put in to produce the OUTLET
magazine. I have been prompted
to join the membership by ALAN
RUTHERFORD, one of your corres-
pondants who shifted here to NEW
ZEALAND last year. After he
advertised for other SPECTRUM
owners in NEW ZEALAND I respond-
ed. As yet we have not met in
person as he resides some 250
miles to the north of me.He made
it possible for me to view some
back issues so I could get an
impression of the high standards
you are able to maintain.


I was aware of your existence as
we have a local SAM owner who
was a subscriber and I had seen
the occasional extract while
visiting him.

Let me introduce my self:my name
is Peter Johnson and I live on
the southern outskirts of the
ciy of Dunedin which is located
on the SE coast of the South
Island of New Zealand. I have a
block of land about 12 acres
where I raise a few sheep (what
else) as a hobby farm. I retired
some six years ago after a full
working life in the broadcasting
industry. When TV was first
introduced to New Zealand some
thirty years ago I was there at
its introduction and remained
there until my retirement.

I am also involved in amateur
radio (not too uncommon for
someone in the technical side of
the work), and have held my
license for about 35 years.
Since I gather there are some
other RADIO AMATEURS within the
membership I will supply my call
sign. It is ZL4LV.

My entry into computers only
came about since my retirement
about six years ago. Because of
my technical background I get a
number of requests to fix it!!!
It started in a small way, with
a request to repair the keyboard
on a ZX81 and since I had no
understanding of the programing
side I had to learn. From there
it has developed.


Currently I've 4 SPECTRUMS in my
electronic workshop along with
the Amateur Radio equipment:

1. A SPECTRUM PLUS equipped with
twin 3.5 in. discs interfaced by
a DISCIPLE. There is also a
MULTIFACE 128 attached.

2. A RUBBER KEY type with INTER-
FACE 1 and MICRDRIVES. This one
has a MULTIPRINT fitted.

3. A GREY 128 +2 equipped with
either a PLUS D and twin 3.5
drives or INTERFACE 1/MICRO-
DRIVES. This also is equipped
with a MULTIFACE 128.

4. A further 48k rubber key type
again equipped with IF1/MDRIVE.


There is provision for a further
two to be added if necessary.
Each computer is equipped with a
small 8" green screen monitor
using direct video feeds. [see
future DRIVECHAT article on this
subject in a future OUTLET - Ed]
There is a larger colour monitor
that can be switched between any
of the SPECTRUMS.


Each of the SPECTRUMS (except
the PLUS D) are linked with the
"NETWORKING" facility: a very
useful feature that I will
elaborate on in the following
material.

What are they all used for? I
will attempt to explain...


SPECTRUMS 1 and 3 are used for
general purpose computing, word
processing, printed circuit
design etc.

SPECTRUM 4 has its main function
as a terminal unit for Amateur
Radio Packet Radio. (For those
who ask "What is PACKET RADIO?"
- put in simple terms it is a
worldwide network of interlinked
bulletin boards using radio
rather than telephone lines.)

SPECTRUM 2 is used mainly as a
program development aid - an
extension to the memory of
SPECTRUM 1.In this case material
is transfered via the NETWORK
for test or evaluation, a crash
means a copy still remains.


With the MULTIFACES and GENIE
disasembler I find it a more
practical way of working. Normal
saves to disc are still made.


The terminal SPECTRUM 4 uses an
RS232 link to interface to a TNC
(This is the abreviation for
TERMINAL NODE CONTROLLER).

The TNC is a dedicated micropro-
cessor-based unit which, in the
one I use, contains a Z80, ROM
and RAM. This in turn is conn-
ected to a two-way VHF radio for
linking to the local bulletin
board. This TNC handles the
special protocols associated
with PACKET RADIO. The SPECTRUM
simply acts as a terminal.


Originally I used the INTERFACE
1 RS232 input/output but this
was less than satisfactory due
to the way Sinclair have
implemented the RS232 function
using software. I now use a home
made RS232 attachment with
vastly improved results. I could
elaborate on the INTERFACE 1
problems but this will take too
long apart from saying that
Version 1 is virtually useless
due to a well-known bug which
causes BREAK whenever SPACE is
pressed.

The terminal SPECTRUM 4 has only
the normal string-handling
facilities which is suitable for
commands and short messages. For
longer text files outgoing these


can be compiled on a wordpro-
cessor and transfered via the
NETWORK for onward transmission.

Incoming messages likewise can
be transfered via the NETWOK for
subsequent saving to disc or
printed out. A further feature
of this Packet Radio system is
that it enables text files to be
transfered between computers of
widely different types eg, IBM
or AMIGA. I have used this
method to send material written
for our New Zealand national
Amateur magazine "BREAK IN"
(nothing to do with burglars)
compiled on the lowly SPECTRUM
and eventually being loaded into
the printers text compiler, no
retyping required.


As you may gather,my interest is
more towards the technical side
of the computer system. I seem
to finish up as Mr. Fixit and as
a result, have acquired a list
of faults and problems that may
be of interest to others. [see a
future DRIVECHAT - Ed]

A request from me to any other
reader who may be able to help.
I have two faulty DISCIPLES.
Here, one is part-functional, no
printer port while the other is
completely non-functional. The
faults in both cases are faulty
PAL chips. The chips are readily
available but need to be
programmed for the particular
application. The questions I ask
are :-


1. Does anyone have or know of a
source of these chips? I have
written to a number of DISCIPLE
repair firms but drawn a blank.
Specifically, I need two PAL DEE
IC9 marked with red and green
dots, and one PAL DUM IC8 marked
with red and yellow dots.

2. Anyone tried to have a copy
made of a good working chip?
FARNEL ELECTRONIC COMPONENTS (I
don't have a UK address) advert-
ise a programming facility. I am

Dear Brian/Ron/Chris,

Re Bill Clark's letter in Outlet No. 80 about 'hidden messages' in the +3 ROM, to arrive at "Test Screen" you first hold down the BREAK key then push the 'Reset' button. Thanks Bill. I had long since forgotten the "test screen" but it now seems to ring a faint bell.

Brian

LPRINT "testing 123";CHR$ 10; CHR$ 13 : BEEP 1,1 :

Dear Ron and Brian,

These run OK on the Spectrum +3 with the +D in 128K mode but not on the 48K Spectrum + or the +3 in 48K mode.Do you know if there is an answer to this problem? Thanks for all the work and the long hours you spend in produc- ing OUTLET.I look forward to its arrival every month and now you are producing a version for the PC I shall look forward with great interest to see the result.I wish you every success.

Brian Cavers to Donald Pemberton

Thanks Donald.

When you load a file from the +3 disc then you must be in 128K mode. If you then snapshot it to the +D, even though you use key 4 to save a 48K snapshot, you're actually saving a 48K image of the machine in 128K mode as well as the registers, flags, error pointer etc for 128K.

The simplest way is to break in and enter RUN 9982 which saves to +D and uses far less space on the disk. If when it reloads off the +D it "hangs" or tries to load from the +3 disc it may be trying to load code, so...

Break in and note the line num- of the break. LIST and examine the line and note the filename of the code. You need to copy that too from the +3 disc to the +D and then REMEMBER to alter the syntax of that line to +D, ie, LOAD d*;"name" CODE. To copy the code you need...

10 CLEAR A-1 10 LOAD "NAME" CODE 20 SAVE d*"NAME" CODE A,L

You need to substitute the true values for A, L and A-1. You may find these in line 9984 in newer issues but otherwise you need a program like CATDB in Issue 76 or EXTENDACAT in 37.

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Ron and Brian.

Your comment about the firm's responsibility ending once they have sent the goods with no obligation to replace or refund if they get lost, once again raises an issue I have been campaigning my MP and consumer groups for some time to get laws changed/introduced to give the consumer (customer) far better protection when dealing with mail order firms. The following is as it seems to me after some years of delving into the subject.

As OUTLET says, CHEZRON takes responsibility for goods that get lost or damaged; larger mail order companies also in the main do the same,the more responsible companies large or small often in the interests of customer relations and to keep their good name will also see the customer right.

However, it seems there is not a legal obligation do do so; it depends on the firm's terms of trading. "WHICH?", and two other magazines, have in recent times printed items that more or less say if the customer does not receive goods that have been sent then tough luck! (put a bit more politely but with same message).

The following extract from the OFFICE OF FAIR trading publi- cation "GET SMART" on mail order says it all.. "If goods get lost after they have been sent to you it is normally your loss depending on on the carriers terms but many firms will bear the loss as a matter of good will."

So once the firm hands goods to the Post Office or any carrier, their responsibility legally ends (unless their terms of trading says otherwise) it seems. Note the above states "carriers terms" so the only course of action if the goods get lost (or damaged) is to claim from the carrier.

Again, this is a minefield as such as the P.O. or Parcelforce have different compensation terms for different services and if the sender did not use an in- sured method of sending then no compensation;also you need proof of posting to make a claim. This would have to be obtained from the sender who probably did not get one when posting.

Depending on the cost of goods, one method would be to make the sender prove they sent the goods perhaps through the County Court but with no guarantee of success as if a person in Manchester bought an item from a firm in London then he would have to go to London as CC hearings are heard near the firm's address.

I have taken issue with the Post Office and also brought the matter to the attention of consumer groups and my MP that while it seems the law says it is the customer's loss and responsibility to make a claim, the Post Office claims form asks a lot of questions that the customer cannot answer -only the sender, ie, time and place of posting,postage paid,how wrapped weight, postal receipt and so on.

To top it all the PO will only pay compensation to the sender unless the sender states in writing otherwise.

I put it to Parcelforce that I pay for goods plus the extra compensation fee to send, the goods get lost, the PO only pays compensation to sender, sender then refuses to replace goods or refund so they have now been paid twice for same goods and the customer still has nothing. "that's quite correct"say Parcel Force, "that's our regulations".

I understand there is some EEC proposal in the pipeline that will make it law that a customer does not have to pay for goods until AFTER they have been received - so no more having to send money with the order.

This will go a long way to prot- ect customers from lost/damaged goods,firms that go bust or dis- appear etc,but could cause prob- lems to small firms who often rely on taking in money before sending goods to pay their way. Plus it could cause problems if people order goods then "avoid" paying. I suspect pressure from firms could well prevent this from becoming law.The problem is "good" firms could well suffer due to the antics of "less good firms". It would certainly stop cases sometimes seen on TV and in papers where it seems a"firm" or individual sets up with the sole intention of taking money but not supplying goods and then doing a runner. .

You often see mentioned to only deal with firms that belong to one of the trading associations or mail order protection schemes but I find far too often the magazine or firm selling what I want - commonly in specialized areas such as computers - do not belong to any such schemes. Also the schemes have so many "get out" clauses you find your case is not covered.

My MP says there is not a big enough problem with mail order firms to change law or introduce better compensation schemes. (A trading Standards Office said they were not interested as I did not pay them my Poll Tax!).

It is only the more spectacular "complaints" that get publicity in the press;only major or crim- inal cases that reach the Office of Fair Trading so,is the extent of the problem really known? If every time an unresolved problem with a mail order firm cropped up, ie, going bust,disappearing, not sending goods, not replacing lost/damaged goods etc resulted in a complaint to an MP, the scale of the problem could well be put into better proportion. I suspect many cases especially if only few pounds are involved,end in the customer suffering in silence as it's not worth taking legal action and no point at all if a firm has gone bust.A letter to an MP only costs a stamp.

The situation therefore seems that if you send for goods by post and actually receive them then think yourself lucky and give a big sigh of relief. If you do not and the firm takes the stand "not our problem" then as said before, tough luck - it seems it was your silly fault to order by mail in the first place. You're on your own unless the firm actually committed a criminal offence then TSO will show some interest, If a civil complaint - then little chance. Even in one case where both the TSO and Advertising Standards both upheld a complaint re a firm and reprimanded them,it did nothing to help my problem or get redress from the firm.

When I send an item by post or any other method I ensure it is covered by some form of insur- ance relative to its value, ie providing you obtain a "receipt of posting",which is free at the PO when you hand the item over, it is covered up to about `22. Higher cost needs special insur- ance. It can often be better to send by Parcelforce + insurance even if small or light enough for ordinary post.Obviously such as OUTLET is impracticable to hand over a hundred discs and ask for a hundred receipts or expect the PO to check a list of 100 addresses. It would also probably cost more in time, effort and extra postage to put in a claim for a lost issue.

When buying anything and I do not know if the sender provides some form of protection or "good will", I try and remember to ask or insist it is covered by insurance even though this may put the cost up.

I have at times also insisted the sender sends me the "proof of posting" or insurance receipt as proof they have sent it. This has also proved beneficial in the past as I have been able to make the claim myself without having to rely on sender.

more....

P.W.JOHNSON, SADDLE HILL ROAD, No. 1 R.D. DUNEDIN, NEW ZEALAND.

Greetings to all the team there from NEW ZEALAND and congratul- ations on the mighty effort you put in to produce the OUTLET magazine. I have been prompted to join the membership by ALAN RUTHERFORD, one of your corres- pondants who shifted here to NEW ZEALAND last year. After he advertised for other SPECTRUM owners in NEW ZEALAND I respond- ed. As yet we have not met in person as he resides some 250 miles to the north of me.He made it possible for me to view some back issues so I could get an impression of the high standards you are able to maintain.

I was aware of your existence as we have a local SAM owner who was a subscriber and I had seen the occasional extract while visiting him.

Let me introduce my self:my name is Peter Johnson and I live on the southern outskirts of the ciy of Dunedin which is located on the SE coast of the South Island of New Zealand. I have a block of land about 12 acres where I raise a few sheep (what else) as a hobby farm. I retired some six years ago after a full working life in the broadcasting industry. When TV was first introduced to New Zealand some thirty years ago I was there at its introduction and remained there until my retirement.

I am also involved in amateur radio (not too uncommon for someone in the technical side of the work), and have held my license for about 35 years. Since I gather there are some other RADIO AMATEURS within the membership I will supply my call sign. It is ZL4LV.

My entry into computers only came about since my retirement about six years ago. Because of my technical background I get a number of requests to fix it!!! It started in a small way, with a request to repair the keyboard on a ZX81 and since I had no understanding of the programing side I had to learn. From there it has developed.

Currently I've 4 SPECTRUMS in my electronic workshop along with the Amateur Radio equipment:

1. A SPECTRUM PLUS equipped with twin 3.5 in. discs interfaced by a DISCIPLE. There is also a MULTIFACE 128 attached.

2. A RUBBER KEY type with INTER- FACE 1 and MICRDRIVES. This one has a MULTIPRINT fitted.

3. A GREY 128 +2 equipped with either a PLUS D and twin 3.5 drives or INTERFACE 1/MICRO- DRIVES. This also is equipped with a MULTIFACE 128.

4. A further 48k rubber key type again equipped with IF1/MDRIVE.

There is provision for a further two to be added if necessary. Each computer is equipped with a small 8" green screen monitor using direct video feeds. [see future DRIVECHAT article on this subject in a future OUTLET - Ed] There is a larger colour monitor that can be switched between any of the SPECTRUMS.

Each of the SPECTRUMS (except the PLUS D) are linked with the "NETWORKING" facility: a very useful feature that I will elaborate on in the following material.

What are they all used for? I will attempt to explain...

SPECTRUMS 1 and 3 are used for general purpose computing, word processing, printed circuit design etc.

SPECTRUM 4 has its main function as a terminal unit for Amateur Radio Packet Radio. (For those who ask "What is PACKET RADIO?" - put in simple terms it is a worldwide network of interlinked bulletin boards using radio rather than telephone lines.)

SPECTRUM 2 is used mainly as a program development aid - an extension to the memory of SPECTRUM 1.In this case material is transfered via the NETWORK for test or evaluation, a crash means a copy still remains.

With the MULTIFACES and GENIE disasembler I find it a more practical way of working. Normal saves to disc are still made.

The terminal SPECTRUM 4 uses an RS232 link to interface to a TNC (This is the abreviation for TERMINAL NODE CONTROLLER).

The TNC is a dedicated micropro- cessor-based unit which, in the one I use, contains a Z80, ROM and RAM. This in turn is conn- ected to a two-way VHF radio for linking to the local bulletin board. This TNC handles the special protocols associated with PACKET RADIO. The SPECTRUM simply acts as a terminal.

Originally I used the INTERFACE 1 RS232 input/output but this was less than satisfactory due to the way Sinclair have implemented the RS232 function using software. I now use a home made RS232 attachment with vastly improved results. I could elaborate on the INTERFACE 1 problems but this will take too long apart from saying that Version 1 is virtually useless due to a well-known bug which causes BREAK whenever SPACE is pressed.

The terminal SPECTRUM 4 has only the normal string-handling facilities which is suitable for commands and short messages. For longer text files outgoing these

can be compiled on a wordpro- cessor and transfered via the NETWORK for onward transmission.

Incoming messages likewise can be transfered via the NETWOK for subsequent saving to disc or printed out. A further feature of this Packet Radio system is that it enables text files to be transfered between computers of widely different types eg, IBM or AMIGA. I have used this method to send material written for our New Zealand national Amateur magazine "BREAK IN" (nothing to do with burglars) compiled on the lowly SPECTRUM and eventually being loaded into the printers text compiler, no retyping required.

As you may gather,my interest is more towards the technical side of the computer system. I seem to finish up as Mr. Fixit and as a result, have acquired a list of faults and problems that may be of interest to others. [see a future DRIVECHAT - Ed]

A request from me to any other reader who may be able to help. I have two faulty DISCIPLES. Here, one is part-functional, no printer port while the other is completely non-functional. The faults in both cases are faulty PAL chips. The chips are readily available but need to be programmed for the particular application. The questions I ask are :-

1. Does anyone have or know of a source of these chips? I have written to a number of DISCIPLE repair firms but drawn a blank. Specifically, I need two PAL DEE IC9 marked with red and green dots, and one PAL DUM IC8 marked with red and yellow dots.

2. Anyone tried to have a copy made of a good working chip? FARNEL ELECTRONIC COMPONENTS (I don't have a UK address) advert- ise a programming facility. I am reluctant to send chips from my one remaining DISCIPLE half way round the world.I know there are copyright laws but surely a copy for replacement purposes in an otherwise useless piece of equ- ipment is stretching the inter- pretation too far?

3 As a last resort, has anyone attempted to work out the logic for the two chips with the ultimate intention of replacing the chips with a circuit board of convential IC's. I have already gone part of the way on this but there is no point in reinventing the wheel if someone else has done this. I do have a copy of the circuit diagram plus a list of addresses used.

If anyone has an answer for me,I suggest a direct letter to me. [See address at top of letter] This would be greatly appreci- ated.

Peter Johnson

Brian Cavers to Peter Johnson

Thanks Peter. It's good to hear from readers on the other side of the world - sort of OUTLET INTERNATIONAL flavour.

I know many of our readers are hardware enthusiasts and fully expect contacts to be made but write again as there is a flow of new blood from month to month and you may hear from others.

Brian.

**От: Bill Coats, STRATHCLYDE**

Уважаемые Brian/Ron/Chris,

По поводу письма Bill Clark в Outlet № 80 о «скрытых сообщениях» в ПЗУ +3: чтобы попасть на «Тестовый экран» (Test Screen), сначала удерживайте клавишу BREAK, а затем нажмите кнопку «Reset». Это экран с разноцветными цифрами на разноцветных фонах. Если теперь нажать одновременно клавиши QAZPLM, вы попадете в заводской «RAM DATA TEST» с предупреждением, что с этого момента ваши диски могут быть повреждены.

### Brian Cavers отвечает Donald Pemberton

Спасибо, Donald.

Когда вы загружаете файл с диска +3, вы неизбежно находитесь в режиме 128K. Если после этого вы делаете снимок (snapshot) на +D, даже нажимая клавишу 4 для сохранения 48K-снапшота, вы на самом деле сохраняете 48K-образ машины в режиме 128K, а также регистры, флаги, указатель ошибок и т.д. для 128K.

Самый простой способ — прервать выполнение (Break) и ввести `RUN 9982`, что сохранит всё на +D и займёт гораздо меньше места на диске. Если при повторной загрузке с +D программа «зависает» или пытается загрузиться с диска +3, возможно, она пытается загрузить машинный код, так что...

Прервите программу по Break и запишите номер строки прерывания. Выполните LIST, изучите строку и запишите имя файла кода. Вам нужно скопировать и его с диска +3 на +D, а затем НЕ ЗАБЫТЬ изменить синтаксис этой строки под +D, то есть: `LOAD d*;"name" CODE`. Чтобы скопировать код, вам понадобится...

```text
10 CLEAR A-1
10 LOAD "NAME" CODE
20 SAVE d*"NAME" CODE A,L
```

Вам нужно подставить реальные значения для A, L и A-1. В более новых выпусках их можно найти в строке 9984, но в других случаях вам потребуется программа вроде CATDB из 76-го номера или EXTENDACAT из 37-го.  
Brian

Ваш комментарий о том, что ответственность фирмы заканчивается сразу после отправки товара и она не обязана заменять его или возвращать деньги в случае утери, снова поднимает тему, по поводу которой я уже некоторое время веду кампанию через своего члена парламента и общества защиты прав потребителей. Вот как выглядит ситуация, судя по тому, что я выяснил за несколько лет изучения вопроса.

Как пишет OUTLET, CHEZRON берёт на себя ответственность за потерянные или повреждённые товары; крупные посылочные компании в основном поступают так же. Более ответственные фирмы, большие или маленькие, часто в интересах отношений с клиентами и ради сохранения доброго имени идут навстречу покупателю.

Однако, похоже, никаких законных обязательств делать это нет; всё зависит от торговых условий самой фирмы. «WHICH?» и ещё два журнала за последнее время напечатали статьи, где прямым текстом говорится: если клиент не получил отправленный товар, то увы, это его проблемы! Так что как только фирма передаёт товар на почту или любому перевозчику, её юридическая ответственность, судя по всему, заканчивается (если только иное не прописано в её торговых условиях). Обратите внимание: сказано «условий перевозчика», то есть единственный вариант действий в случае утери (или повреждения) товара — требовать возмещения с перевозчика.

Но и тут сплошные подводные камни, поскольку у тех же Post Office или Parcelforce разные условия компенсации для разных услуг. Его придётся получать у отправителя, который, скорее всего, никакого подтверждения при отправке не взял.

В зависимости от стоимости товара, одним из способов было бы заставить отправителя доказать факт отправки через суд графства (County Court), но без всякой гарантии успеха, ведь если житель Манчестера купил товар у лондонской фирмы, ему пришлось бы ехать в Лондон, так как слушания в суде графства проходят по месту нахождения ответчика.

Например: время и место отправки, уплаченный почтовый сбор, упаковка, вес, почтовая квитанция и так далее.

В довершение всего, почта выплачивает компенсацию только отправителю, если только он в письменной форме не укажет иное.

Проблема в том, что «хорошие» компании могут пострадать из-за выходок «менее хороших». Зато это определенно положило бы конец случаям, о которых порой говорят по ТВ и в газетах, когда некая «фирма» или частное лицо создаются лишь с одной целью — собрать деньги, ничего не отправлять и смыться.

Часто советуют иметь дело только с фирмами, состоящими в торговых ассоциациях или системах защиты покупателей по почте, но я сплошь и рядом сталкиваюсь с тем, что журнал или фирма, продающая то, что мне нужно (особенно в таких специализированных областях, как компьютеры), ни в каких подобных схемах не участвуют. Кроме того, в этих схемах столько пунктов мелким шрифтом, позволяющих им снять с себя ответственность, что ваш случай наверняка окажется нестраховым.

Мой депутат в парламенте (MP) утверждает, что проблемы с фирмами почтовой торговли недостаточно масштабны, чтобы менять законодательство или вводить более эффективные системы компенсаций. (А в Trading Standards Office мне и вовсе заявили, что я им не интересен, так как не плачу им свой Poll Tax!).

Огласку в прессе получают лишь самые вопиющие «жалобы»; и только крупные или откровенно уголовные дела доходят до Office of Fair Trading. Так известен ли реальный масштаб бедствия? Если бы каждый раз, когда возникает нерешенная проблема с посылторгом (то есть банкротство, исчезновение, неотправка товара, отказ возместить утерянное/поврежденное и т. д.), люди направляли жалобу своему депутату, масштаб проблемы стал бы куда очевиднее. Подозреваю, что многие — особенно если речь идет о нескольких фунтах — предпочитают молча проглотить обиду: судиться себе дороже, а уж если фирма лопнула, то и вовсе бессмысленно. А ведь письмо депутату стоит всего одну марку.

Поэтому ситуация такова: если вы заказываете что-то по почте и действительно это получаете — считайте, вам повезло, и вздохните с облегчением. Если же нет, а фирма встает в позу «это не наши проблемы», то, как уже говорилось, не обессудьте: выходит, вы сами виноваты, что вообще связались с почтовым заказом. Вы остаетесь один на один со своей бедой, если только фирма не совершила уголовное преступление — тогда TSO проявит хоть какой-то интерес. Если же иск гражданский — шансов мало. Даже в одном случае, когда и TSO, и Advertising Standards удовлетворили жалобу на фирму и вынесли ей выговор, это ни на грамм не помогло решить мою проблему и получить возмещение ущерба.

Когда я сам отправляю что-то почтой или любым другим способом, я всегда слежу за тем, чтобы посылка была застрахована соразмерно ее стоимости. То есть при наличии «квитанции об отправке» (receipt of posting), которую бесплатно выдают на почте при приеме посылки, она застрахована примерно до £22. Для более дорогих вещей нужна специальная страховка. Зачастую лучше отправить через Parcelforce со страховкой, даже если вещь мелкая или достаточно легкая для обычной почты. Разумеется, для кого-то вроде OUTLET нереально прийти с сотней дисков и требовать сотню квитанций или ждать, что почта станет сверять список из 100 адресов. Да и подача иска за утерянный номер, вероятно, отнимет больше времени, сил и почтовых расходов, чем он стоит.

Покупая что-либо, если я не знаю, предоставляет ли отправитель страховку или гарантию «доброй воли», я стараюсь не забывать спросить или потребовать, чтобы посылка была застрахована, даже если это увеличит расходы.

Иногда я также настаивал, чтобы отправитель присылал мне «proof of posting» или страховую квитанцию в качестве подтверждения отправки. В прошлом это не раз выручало: я мог подать претензию сам, не полагаясь на милость отправителя.

Все SPECTRUM (кроме того, что с PLUS D) соединены посредством сети NETWORKING — исключительно полезная функция, о которой я подробнее расскажу далее.

Для чего все они используются? Попробую объяснить...

SPECTRUM №1 и №3 используются для задач общего назначения, текстовой обработки, проектирования печатных плат и т. д.

SPECTRUM №4 в основном служит терминалом для радиолюбительской пакетной связи Packet Radio. (Для тех, кто спросит: «Что такое PACKET RADIO?» — проще говоря, это всемирная сеть объединенных BBS, работающая по радио, а не по телефонным линиям).

SPECTRUM №2 используется главным образом как подспорье в разработке программ — своего рода расширение памяти для SPECTRUM №1. В этом случае данные передаются по сети NETWORK для тестирования или отладки: если система зависнет, копия все равно останется целой.

В связке с MULTIFACE и дизассемблером GENIE такой метод работы кажется мне куда более практичным. Обычные сохранения на диск при этом никто не отменял.

Терминальный SPECTRUM 4 использует RS232-соединение для связи с TNC (это сокращение от TERMINAL NODE CONTROLLER).

TNC — это специализированный блок на базе микропроцессора, который в моём случае содержит Z80, ROM и RAM. Он, в свою очередь, подключен к двусторонней УКВ-радиостанции для связи с местной доской объявлений (BBS). Этот TNC обрабатывает специальные протоколы, связанные с PACKET RADIO. Сам SPECTRUM выступает просто в качестве терминала.

Изначально я использовал ввод/вывод RS232 от INTERFACE 1, но это было далеко не идеально из-за того, как Sinclair реализовали функцию RS232 программным способом. Сейчас я использую самодельную приставку RS232 со значительно лучшими результатами. Я мог бы подробно описать проблемы с INTERFACE 1, но это займет слишком много времени; скажу лишь, что Version 1 практически непригодна к использованию из-за общеизвестной ошибки, которая вызывает BREAK при каждом нажатии SPACE.

Терминальный SPECTRUM 4 имеет лишь обычные средства обработки строк, что подходит для команд и коротких сообщений. Для более длинных исходящих текстовых файлов их можно набрать в текстовом процессоре и переслать по NETWORK для дальнейшей передачи в эфир.

Входящие сообщения точно так же можно пересылать по NETWORK для последующего сохранения на диск или вывода на печать. Еще одна особенность этой системы Packet Radio заключается в том, что она позволяет передавать текстовые файлы между совершенно разными типами компьютеров, например, IBM или AMIGA.
